title: PowerUp Money raises $10M to expand AI-led wealth management
summary: PowerUp Money raises 10 million dollars to expand its AI driven wealth management platform
detailed: PowerUp Money, a wealthtech platform offering mutual fund advice and digital wealth management services, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, an early-stage investment firm.
The Bengaluru-based company plans to use a significant portion of the capital to develop its AI-powered wealth management platform and expand its managed advisory business.

Founder and chief executive officer Prateek Jindal said, “AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally”, bringing personalised guidance within reach of investors who may not be able to afford traditional wealth management services.
Debt investment platform Wint Wealth raised Rs 250 crore in a Series B round in January, while wealth management firm Centricity secured Rs 280 crore in August.
sentences: PowerUp Money, a wealthtech platform offering mutual fund advice and digital wealth management services, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, an early-stage investment firm.
Existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC also participated.
The Bengaluru-based company plans to use a significant portion of the capital to develop its AI-powered wealth management platform and expand its managed advisory business.
PowerUp claims more than 1.5 million users track mutual fund portfolios worth over Rs 2.5 lakh crore on its platform.
Its paid subscription service, Elite, provides research-backed mutual fund advice and is said to have crossed 1,00,000 paid members in less than a year.
The company has now introduced Elite Prime, an AI-enabled digital wealth advisory service designed to provide a more comprehensive financial planning experience.

It assesses investors’ financial goals, risk appetite and existing holdings to suggest asset allocation, systematic investment plans (SIPs), lump-sum investments, portfolio rebalancing and withdrawal strategies.
It can also identify gaps in portfolios and suggest diversification into assets such as gold, silver and international investments.
An AI wealth coach and personal assistant are intended to help users understand recommendations and make informed decisions.

Founder and chief executive officer Prateek Jindal said, “AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally”, bringing personalised guidance within reach of investors who may not be able to afford traditional wealth management services.
PowerUp is also looking to expand Infinite, its managed wealth advisory offering.
The service combines financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation and ongoing portfolio management with dedicated human advisers.
According to the company, Infinite has accumulated nearly Rs 500 crore in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch, despite being available to a limited customer base.
Making the service accessible to more investors is another priority for the new funding.
The expansion comes amid sustained growth in India’s mutual fund market.
According to the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI), industry AUM stood at Rs 82.64 lakh crore at the end of September 2026, up from Rs 15.8 lakh crore a decade earlier.
Monthly SIP contributions also reached Rs 32,490 crore in September, reflecting the growing adoption of regular, long-term investing.
Investor interest has encouraged further funding across the wealthtech sector.
Debt investment platform Wint Wealth raised Rs 250 crore in a Series B round in January, while wealth management firm Centricity secured Rs 280 crore in August.
AI-focused advisory startup Novelty Wealth also announced a $1.4 million seed round in March.
However, growth brings its own challenges.
Digital advice must remain suitable, transparent and compliant as platforms expand their customer base.
SEBI issued an updated Master Circular for Investment Advisers in February, reinforcing the regulatory framework governing investment advice.
The opportunity, as Flourish Ventures’ Asia head Ravi Kaushik noted, lies in helping investors manage increasingly complex financial lives.
